requirements.title: The /graph page shall open a side panel showing page detail when a visitor clicks a node

vision.paraphrase: Side panel on node click shows page detail and GitHub source link for transparency.
Side panel displays page detail and GitHub source link when a node is clicked.

conops.paraphrase: After clicking a node, a side panel opens showing page detail and GitHub source link.
Clicking a node triggers the side panel to open.

requirements.title: The side panel shall populate with page detail without triggering a full page navigation, keeping the graph visible and in its current center/zoom state

amended.reason: Originally specified as a slide-in overlay panel. The shipped design instead renders the side panel as an always-visible flex column that populates with content on node click, rather than sliding in. This was an explicit, live product decision made during epic scQi8pt — a cross-epic amendment to this epic's (V3PlLFL) requirement.

vision.paraphrase: Side panel populates with page detail without full page navigation, keeping graph context visible during exploration.

conops.paraphrase: The side panel populates with content while the graph remains visible in its current state.

requirements.title: The side panel shall return to its placeholder state when the visitor explicitly dismisses the selected node, returning full focus to the graph canvas

amended.reason: Originally specified as a slide-in overlay that closes/unmounts on dismiss. The shipped design keeps the side panel permanently mounted as an always-visible column, so dismissing reverts it to its placeholder text rather than closing the panel. Cross-epic amendment to this epic's (V3PlLFL) requirement, made during epic scQi8pt.

vision.paraphrase: The panel is described as populating 'without a full page navigation, keeping graph context visible' — a dismiss action returns the panel to its placeholder state so the visitor can return to unobstructed graph exploration.

requirements.title: The side panel shall display the node's title, tags, and status dot

vision.paraphrase: Side panel displays page detail including title, tags, and status.

conops.paraphrase: Side panel shows page title, tags, status dot, and related-node list.
The side panel displays page title, tags, and status dot.

requirements.title: The side panel shall display a list of the node's related nodes derived from its graph edges

conops.paraphrase: Side panel lists each directly connected related node.
The side panel shows a list of related nodes.

requirements.title: The side panel shall display a "View source on GitHub" link that opens the raw Markdown file for that page in a new tab

vision.paraphrase: Source transparency requires a working link to the page's raw Markdown source on GitHub for verification.
Side panel includes a GitHub source link to the raw .md file.

conops.paraphrase: Side panel displays a 'View source on GitHub' link to the raw .md file.
Side panel shows a 'View source on GitHub' link that opens the raw .md file.

requirements.title: The side panel shall preserve its open state and displayed content when a visitor returns to the /graph browser tab after visiting the GitHub source link in a separate tab

conops.paraphrase: After visiting the GitHub source link in a new tab and returning to the graph tab, the side panel remains open showing the same node's detail.

requirements.title: The side panel shall display a folder badge for the selected node, colored to match that folder's color in the graph

vision.paraphrase: The browsable detail panel includes a colored folder badge to ground the node in its taxonomy and reinforce visual connections to the graph.

conops.paraphrase: The side panel displays a folder badge colored to match the node's folder/taxonomy cluster, making the node's content category immediately clear.

requirements.title: The side panel shall display the selected node's description from graph-data.json

vision.paraphrase: The browsable detail panel displays the per-page description (frontmatter or first-paragraph fallback) to provide quick context without visiting the source.

conops.paraphrase: When the side panel opens, it displays the node's description field, giving the visitor a 1–3 sentence summary of the page's content.

requirements.title: The side panel shall omit the description area entirely, without rendering an empty gap or placeholder, when the selected node's description is empty

conops.paraphrase: When a node has no description, the side panel omits the description area cleanly without rendering empty space, keeping the layout tight.

requirements.title: The side panel shall render the selected node's connected pages as clickable chips grouped under their folder/taxonomy headings

vision.paraphrase: The browsable detail panel's connected-page chips enable navigation by making related nodes immediately clickable, turning the panel into an active exploration surface.

conops.paraphrase: The side panel lists connected pages as clickable chips grouped by their folder/taxonomy, allowing easy navigation to related content.

requirements.title: The side panel shall select the target node, updating both the graph focus and the panel content, when a visitor clicks a connected-page chip

vision.paraphrase: Connected-page chips are not just labels but navigable elements; clicking a chip selects that node and updates the panel, making the side panel an active navigation tool.

conops.paraphrase: When a visitor clicks a connected-page chip, that node becomes selected; the graph focuses on it (center/zoom or connector animation per mode) and the panel updates to show its detail.

requirements.title: The side panel's "View source on GitHub" link shall resolve to an existing file for every node in the deployed public vault build

vision.paraphrase: Source transparency actually works when source links resolve; fixing issue #4 finding A3 ensures every node's GitHub link leads to a real page.
The repo goes public (after a history audit) so source links resolve for anonymous visitors, closing the loop on the transparency promise.

conops.paraphrase: When a visitor clicks the GitHub source link, the URL resolves to the actual raw .md file in the public repository (contingent on the repo being public per TOR-10-vaZLdHp).

requirements.title: The side panel shall display a "Cited sources" list of clickable links when the selected node's sourceLinks field is non-empty

vision.paraphrase: The side panel additionally lists up to 5 externally-cited links found inline in a page's body Markdown, distinct from the single self-referential GitHub source link.

vision.section: §6 — MVP Scope Summary (Body Source Links, Cycle 4)
vision.paraphrase: When a node has one or more sourceLinks, the side panel renders a Cited sources list of clickable links opening in a new tab, using the same visual treatment as the GitHub source link.
The cited-sources list renders below the existing connected-pages section in the side panel, maintaining visual consistency with other source-transparency affordances.

conops.paraphrase: When a visitor clicks a node, the side panel displays the node's detail including a cited-sources list if the page has extracted body links.
The cited-sources list appears below the connected-pages section showing up to 5 clickable links labeled with their Markdown text, in document order.

requirements.title: The side panel shall omit the "Cited sources" section entirely, without rendering an empty heading or placeholder, when the selected node's sourceLinks field is empty

vision.section: §6 — MVP Scope Summary (Body Source Links, Cycle 4)
vision.paraphrase: When a node has zero sourceLinks, the cited-sources section is omitted entirely without an empty list or placeholder, mirroring the existing empty-description precedent.
The side panel omits the cited-sources section entirely when a page has no body links, allowing clean layout without empty sections.

conops.paraphrase: The side panel omits description and cited-sources areas entirely when they are empty, keeping the layout tight and focused on available content.
When a visitor clicks a node with no inline body links, the cited-sources section does not render at all, and the panel displays remaining detail normally.

requirements.title: Each cited-source link shall open its target URL in a new tab

vision.section: §6 — MVP Scope Summary (Body Source Links, Cycle 4)
vision.paraphrase: Cited-source links open in a new tab, using the same interaction pattern as the GitHub source link to maintain consistent behavior across all source-transparency affordances.

conops.paraphrase: When a visitor clicks a cited-source link, it opens in a new tab, allowing them to verify the external material cited by the page without losing the graph context.
